page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R32 processor clocked at 3.3 GHz, it features 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. For high-speed local scratch space, it includes a bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest computational and memory throughput. In stress-ng evaluations, the server produced single-core and multi-core scores in the bottom 10 percent of tested configurations. Geekbench testing returned a single-core score of 1325.0, reflecting average performance, while the multi-core score of 3059.0 ranked in the bottom 25 percent. Cryptographic operations show greater strength due to hardware acceleration flags, with PassMark CPU encryption tests landing in the middle 50 percent alongside moderate gzip compression throughput. However, general memory performance remains low, with PassMark memory testing ranking in the bottom 10 percent and uncached 256 MB memory write bandwidth reaching 22.34 GB/sec.

The inclusion of direct-attached NVMe storage provides low-latency local I/O without incurring external block storage network overhead. However, the limited 8.0 GB memory footprint and low multi-core throughput constrain high-concurrency tasks. Application workloads requiring heavy parallelism or deep cache hierarchies will face performance ceilings, as seen in weak Clang compilation and static web serving throughput benchmarks.

The c5ad.xlarge instance fits compute-focused tasks requiring rapid, ephemeral local disk operations. Best-fit workloads include distributed build workers, continuous integration testing, batch data manipulation, lightweight web servers, and processing pipelines where scratch space latency is critical but overall RAM demands remain low.
description: Amazon Web Services c5ad.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor clocked at 3.3 GHz. The instance provisions 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD for fast local storage, paired with 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no GPU resources. Performance benchmarks position the instance within the mid-tier for single-threaded tasks and encryption routines, though multi-core processing and memory subsystem benchmarks rank in the lower quartiles. The primary engineering tradeoff is high-speed, direct-attached ephemeral storage combined with a restricted 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The c5ad.xlarge is best suited for build pipelines, CI/CD runners, batch file processing, and lightweight services that require fast local disk caching.
